note: RECONCILED 2026-09-07 (CTX-B dispatch, operator-ruled) between this repo's prior 4-district Article-II-single-family-only table and legacy-design-tools' independently-researched 10-district table, both derived from City of Round Rock Zoning and Development Code, Code of Ordinances Part III (2018 Edition), Chapter 2, Article II (Residential Districts), Section 2-26 (Residential Lot and Building Dimensional Standards), retrieved via https://roundrock-tx.elaws.us/code/coor_ptiii_ch2_artii_sec2-26 (Round Rock's own library.municode.com pages return HTTP 403 to automated fetch; no field here reaches human-verified against a real code-section atom -- round_rock_tx has 361 real atoms and Sections 1-50/2-26 both exist as real ingested atoms, but neither atom's bodyText captures the dimensional-standards chart's actual cell values, a table-extraction gap, not a corpus absence -- so every field here is primary-source-verified). RULING 1 (side_corner_ft, ALL 10 districts): this repo's DERIVATION wins over the other table's assumption. Chapter 1 definitions, Section 1-50 ('Front Lot Line'), state 'In cases where two or more lot lines abut an existing or dedicated street, all such lot lines are considered front lot lines for the purposes of calculating building setbacks' -- a general Chapter 1 rule, not limited to Article II's single-family rows -- so side_corner_ft = front_ft on every district Article II tabulates no separate corner figure for. The other table instead mirrored the base side setback (an unmotivated assumption, and the permissive/smaller-setback direction for a buildable envelope) on all 10 districts; that reasoning is superseded here. One district, TH (Townhouse, Single-lot), is the exception: Section 2-26's own row tabulates an explicit adjacent-to-street side value ('5 ft./20 ft.' interior/adjacent-to-street) rather than leaving a blank cell for Section 1-50 to fill, so TH's side_corner_ft is that directly-tabulated 20 ft, not a Section-1-50 derivation off its 15 ft front_ft (the other table's own provenance quote already named this 20 ft value but the table's stored side_corner_ft field left it at 5, mirroring side_ft instead -- a bug, corrected here, not a re-derivation). RULING 1 AMENDMENT (2026-09-07, second review): MF-2 was flagged, then resolved. Applying the derivation there would produce 15 ft, LOOSER than the superseded side-mirror convention's 25 ft (MF-2 is the only district where front_ft < side_ft, so the derivation loosens instead of tightens). A derivation is trustworthy when it tightens a figure (safe if the underlying legal reasoning turns out imprecise) and is NOT sufficient on its own when it loosens one (unsafe if wrong) -- so MF-2's side_corner_ft is REFUSED rather than derived: no primary-source citation was found for a distinct MF-2 corner value, and 25 ft (the more conservative candidate) is carried as a not_specified placeholder pending one. Every other district's derivation was checked against this same tighten/loosen test and tightens (or, for SR, is unchanged): none of the other 9 needed this exception. RULING 2 (district breadth): all 10 districts (SF-R, SF-1, SF-2, SF-3, MH, TF, TH, SR, MF-1, MF-2) are carried, not just the 4 this file previously shipped -- six districts do not fall to absence. RULING 3 (SF-3 side_ft/rear_ft): REFUSED, not picked. The two source tables read different, genuinely different sub-columns of the same Section 2-26 SF-3 chart cell -- this file's prior research read the zero-lot-line option (side_ft=12, rear_ft=15), the other table read the Standard-Lot sub-column (side_ft=5, rear_ft=10) -- and a parcel's GIS zoningCode of 'SF-3' cannot distinguish which sub-type actually applies on the ground. Both are defensible, differently-reasoned readings of the same table cell, not an error on either side. side_ft and rear_ft below carry the zero-lot-line reading (12/15, the larger, more conservative pair) ONLY as a required-by-schema numeric placeholder, flagged not_specified: true with an explicit refusal quote -- a correct reader must treat SF-3's side_ft/rear_ft as unresolved pending a real per-parcel sub-type read, not as a settled value. RULING 4 (max_height_ft sentinel): unified to 999 (this file's prior value) across all districts, not 100 (the other table's prior value) -- both were flagged not_specified: true, but 999 cannot be mistaken for a real building height in feet the way 100 (a physically plausible height for some multifamily district) can, and — as originally written here — 'this repo's gate.ts enforces the 999 sentinel by rule G7 whenever not_specified is set on max_height_ft, so the invariant is checked in code, not left to a convention.' [P-258 LANE-C CORRECTION (2026-09-16, branch seat/p258-lane-c): the quoted sentence above is TRUE of hauska-setback-corpus — whose gate.ts does define rule G7 (rule union includes G7; its own implementation is commented 'G7 — max_height_ft's not_specified sentinel must be the ONE canonical value (999)'; NOT_SPECIFIED_MAX_HEIGHT_FT = 999; unit-tested in src/setbacks/__tests__/gate.test.ts) and DOES block a not_specified max_height_ft that is not 999 — and FALSE of legacy-design-tools, the other repo this same file lives in, whose own gate.ts has no G7 at all (rule union G1|G2|G3|G4|G5|G6). So in legacy-design-tools the 999 invariant is a convention plus this file's test, not a code-enforced rule, and the original sentence must not be read as a repo-independent statement. SECOND CORRECTION, because it was asserted to this lane during review and is wrong: 999 is NOT emitted as a G3 out-of-band flag on these cells. G3's sanity-band check is guarded by 'if (!isNotSpecified)' in BOTH gate.ts files, so a cell whose provenance sets not_specified: true never reaches the [0, 300] band test. The unified 999 value itself is unchanged and not in question — only the claim about where the rule lives was wrong.] front_ft/rear_ft/side_ft/max_lot_coverage_pct/max_impervious_pct for SF-R/SF-1/SF-2 and MH/TF/TH/SR/MF-1/MF-2 (the non-SF-3 rows) are unchanged from whichever source table alone: SF-R/SF-1/SF-2 core dimensional cells were the two source tables' one point of full agreement; MH/TF/TH/SR/MF-1/MF-2 were carried from legacy-design-tools' table (this file did not previously ship them). P-258 LANE-C ADDENDUM (2026-09-16, acquisition campaign, branch seat/p258-lane-c): 14 commercial, employment/industrial, public/civic and mixed-use districts added from the SAME instrument this table already cites -- City of Round Rock Code of Ordinances, Part III (Zoning and Development Code), Chapter 2 (Zoning Districts and Use Regulations), Sections 2-36 (commercial), 2-49 (employment and industrial), 2-61 (public and civic use) and 2-78 (mixed-use and PUD) -- read this pass from the Municode publication at https://library.municode.com/tx/round_rock/codes/code_of_ordinances?nodeId=PTIIIZODECO_CH2ZODIUSRE (the chapter page carries every chart in one document; the four charts were expanded and read at source on 2026-09-16). WHY THIS PASS SUCCEEDED WHERE EARLIER ONES DID NOT: Round Rock's Municode pages return HTTP 403 to plain automated fetches, and elaws.us (American Legal) timed out on every attempt this session. The charts were read through a real browser session against the Municode page and the rendered text was quoted verbatim; every quote below is copied from that rendering. ADDED: C-1, C-1a, C-2 (Sec. 2-36); OF-1, BP, LI, I (Sec. 2-49); PF-1, PF-2, PF-3 (Sec. 2-61); MU-1, MU-2, MU-L, MU-R (Sec. 2-78). TWO MAPPING RULES USED, BOTH STATED OPENLY. (1) CORNER SETBACK: none of these four charts has a separate corner/street-side column, so side_corner_ft mirrors front_ft on every added row. That is this file's own established derivation for Round Rock (see the reconciliation note above): Chapter 1, Sec. 1-50 'Front Lot Line' states 'In cases where two or more lot lines abut an existing or dedicated street, all such lot lines are considered front lot lines for the purposes of calculating building setbacks', so a corner lot's street-side yard is a front yard. It is flagged derived_from_front_rule in provenance on every added row rather than presented as tabulated. (2) RESIDENTIAL-ADJACENCY ESCALATIONS ARE NOT THE BASE: the LI row's chart prints residential-adjacency escalations (100 ft. rear with a precast panel fence, 80 ft. with masonry; the same for side, and 50 ft./40 ft. for the commercial and public charts) that apply only where a lot abuts SF/TF property and only given a specific fence election. Those are quoted in provenance and are NOT codified as the base rear/side figures, matching how this file already treats conditional adjacencies. THE MIXED-USE CHARTS STATE MAXIMUM FRONT SETBACKS (BUILD-TO LINES), NOT MINIMUMS -- READ CAREFULLY, NOT TRANSCRIBED BLINDLY: Sec. 2-78's first row is 'Maximum front setback from street (ROW)'. Codifying a maximum as front_ft would invert the rule (it would push buildings back instead of holding them to the street), so for MU-1, MU-2 and MU-R front_ft is codified as 0 -- the true minimum, because those districts state no minimum front yard and a building placed anywhere inside the build-to line is compliant -- with the actual maximum quoted verbatim in each row's provenance so the build-to obligation is not lost. MU-L is the exception and carries front_ft 15, because its cell states an express minimum ('Minimum shall be no less than 15 ft.') alongside the 25 ft. maximum; that parse is flagged at 0.7 confidence and the full cell is quoted so a reviewer can overrule it. HEIGHTS: this code states non-residential heights in STORIES in these charts (C-1/C-1a 5, C-2 2, OF-1 2, BP 5, LI 2, I 1, PF-1 2, PF-2 2, PF-3 5), with no feet conversion anywhere in the chart, so max_height_ft is not_specified with the established 100 sentinel on those rows and the stories figure is carried verbatim in the quote -- the governing limit is still enforced, it simply is not a feet scalar. Three added rows DO carry a real feet cap: MU-1 48 ft. ('48 ft. not to exceed 3 stories'), MU-L 35 ft. ('35 ft. not to exceed 2.5 stories') and MU-R 50 ft. ('3 stories/50 ft.'). MU-2 has no single figure at all: its chart cell says 'See Sec. 2-72(d)(7). Height based on building type and location within the district', and Sec. 2-72's maximum-height table is keyed by area (12 stories/160 ft. for the IH-35 frontage-road north lots, an area-specific table for the Round Rock Avenue corridor, etc.), so MU-2 height is not_specified (100 sentinel) with that second citation quoted. MAXIMUM HEIGHT OF ACCESSORY BUILDING (15 ft. in the commercial, employment and public charts) IS A DIFFERENT STRUCTURE CLASS and is not substituted into max_height_ft on any row. IMPERVIOUS / LOT COVERAGE: none of these four charts states a per-district impervious-cover or building-coverage figure (the charts' columns are lot width, street/rear/side setbacks, accessory-building setback, and heights; Sec. 2-26's residential chart is the same). Both max_lot_coverage_pct and max_impervious_pct are therefore not_specified with the 100 sentinel on all 14 rows, with that absence stated in each row's provenance. NOT ROWED, WITH EVIDENCE (the two remaining lane-c codes in this city): (a) UNZ (66 parcels) IS NOT A ZONING DISTRICT and correctly gets no row. Sec. 2-3 'Treatment of property without a zoning classification' states: 'Property that was annexed without a zoning classification, or property existing within the city limits without a zoning classification, shall be treated as follows: (a) A parcel of land that is less than ten acres shall be treated as if it were zoned SF-R (Single-family - Rural); and (b) A parcel of land that is ten acres or more shall be treated as if it were zoned AG (Agricultural).' The layer's 'UNZ' value is therefore a DATA-ABSENCE marker, not a district, and its legal effect is already covered for sub-ten-acre parcels by this table's existing SF-R row. NAMED GAP THIS EXPOSES: the ten-acre-or-more case resolves to AG, and this table has NO AG row -- Round Rock's AG dimensional standards are in the Sec. 2-26 residential chart (AG column: minimum lot area 10 acres, minimum lot width 200 ft., minimum setback from street (ROW) 50 ft., minimum rear setback 50 ft., minimum side setback 20 ft., minimum garage setback from street (ROW) 50 ft.), but the chart's flattened rendering carries subtype sub-headers ('Conventional', 'Zero Lot Line', 'Village', 'Residential Estate Lot', 'Standard Lot', 'Small Lot', 'Single-lot (fee simple units)', 'Common-lot') across twelve district columns, and this pass could NOT resolve that column alignment with confidence. Per the campaign's rule, an unresolved alignment is a gap, not a row: AG is recorded as BLOCKED rather than guessed, and the values above are recorded here only as the shape of what the AG row should contain. (b) SFD / SF-D (87 parcels) IS A DISTRICT, and its front setback is genuinely non-scalar. Round Rock's SF-D (Single-Family - Downtown) district appears in the Sec. 2-26 residential chart whose row 'Minimum setback from street (ROW)' prints 'Contextual' for SF-D, and Sec. 2-17's supplementary note states 'The front setback from the street shall be the same as adjacent buildings +/- 5 feet. If the two setbacks on either side of the subject property are greater than 10 feet different from one another ...'. A contextual front yard is a relationship to neighbours, not a feet figure, so no front_ft can be written honestly for SF-D -- it is recorded BLOCKED with that citation. (c) OS / Open Space (37 parcels) states NO dimensional standards at all, so no row is written. Sec. 2-59 gives only a purpose, the permitted-uses cross-reference to Sec. 2-60, and supplementary screening/outdoor-storage rules; Sec. 2-61's dimensional chart covers PF-1, PF-2 and PF-3 and does NOT list OS. There is nothing to transcribe -- recorded BLOCKED with that citation rather than filled with sentinels that would look like data. SOURCES TRIED: Municode/current official publication (READ this pass via a browser session -- the source of every value above); elaws.us / American Legal (fetch timed out repeatedly, 2026-09-16); Zoneomics code mirror (text read; carries the district roster and the compatibility-buffer rules but no dimensional charts); onlyplans.io district summary (read; itself records that Round Rock's 'Part III Ch. 2 district tables require browser-based retrieval', which matched this pass's experience); Round Rock's own roundrocktexas.gov Development Code page (read for the district roster and the 2023 consolidated-code history). ArcGIS REST was not queried: the level-c gap here was ordinance text, not the zoning map. P-299 OT-2 (2026-09-17): this table's 168 primary-source-verified value slots are RELABELLED to "transcription-read", the fourth verification state added to gate.ts in the same change, with confidence capped at 0.75 (rule G9). Reason, from this file's own note above: every value here was read through a COPY of the governing instrument rather than off the instrument's own text -- the eLaws mirror of the Code of Ordinances (the city's own library.municode.com pages return HTTP 403 to fetch). The state is not a downgrade of the read's quality; it is the honest name for the channel, and it keeps "primary-source-verified" meaning what it says for the tables that did reach the instrument's own text. It is treated exactly like primary-source-verified for rule G2 (no code-section atom is required) and skips G5's quote round-trip for the same reason.
